prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Conroe, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1422; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is about the collision you reported in a parking lot in Conroe, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the address where you currently live.

A: [Claimant name and address on file]

Q: Thank you. Can you walk me through what happened when the collision occurred?

A: I was pulling out of a parking space near the store entrance. I checked my mirror and started backing slowly. I felt a bump and heard a crunch, and when I stopped, I saw the other car had hit the rear passenger side of my vehicle.

Q: Were you moving at the time, and how fast would you estimate you were going?

A: I was barely moving, maybe walking speed. I had not gotten far out of the space yet.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?

A: No, not until right before it hit. I think it was coming down the aisle behind me.

Q: Did you notice any injuries right after the collision?

A: My right shoulder jolted when I was hit, and it started aching within a few minutes. I didn't think much of it at first.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment since the collision?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They took x-rays and told me to follow up with my doctor for the shoulder.

Q: Are you currently receiving any ongoing treatment or therapy?

A: Yes, I have a follow-up appointment scheduled and I've been doing some physical therapy exercises at home.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car repaired and get my shoulder back to normal.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the recorded statement.
